arxiv-2101-05235.title: Space-Efficient Algorithms for Reachability in Directed Geometric Graphs
arxiv-2101-05235.creator: Sujoy Bhore, Rahul Jain
arxiv-2101-05235.description: Abstract The problem of graph Reachability is to decide whether there is a path from one vertex to another in a given graph. In this paper, we study the Reachability problem on three distinct graph families - intersection graphs of Jordan regions, unit contact disk graphs (penny graphs), and chordal graphs.

arxiv-2307-11137.title: Of Models and Tin Men- A behavioural economics study of principal-agent problems in AI alignment using large-language models
arxiv-2307-11137.creator: Steve Phelps, Rebecca Ranson
arxiv-2307-11137.description: Abstract AI Alignment is often presented as an interaction between a single designer and an artificial agent in which the designer attempts to ensure the agent’s behavior is consistent with its purpose, and risks arise solely because of conflicts caused by inadvertent misalignment between the utility function intended by the designer and the resulting internal utility function of the agent.

arxiv-2411-00641.title: Diffusion with preferential relocation in a confining potential
arxiv-2411-00641.creator: Satya N. Majumdar
arxiv-2411-00641.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Satya N. Majumdar. We study the relaxation of a diffusive particle confined in an arbitrary external potential and subject to a non-Markovian resetting protocol. With a constant rate r r , a previous time τ \tau between the initial time and the present time t t is chosen from a given probability distribution K ⁡ ( τ , t ) K(\tau,t) , and the particle is reset to the position that it occupied at time τ \tau .

arxiv-2411-19544.title: SkelMamba: A State Space Model for Efficient Skeleton Action Recognition of Neurological Disorders
arxiv-2411-19544.creator: Niki Martinel, Mariano Serrao, Christian Micheloni
arxiv-2411-19544.description: Abstract We introduce a novel state-space model (SSM)-based framework for skeleton-based human action recognition, with an anatomically-guided architecture that improves state-of-the-art performance in both clinical diagnostics and general action recognition tasks. Our approach decomposes skeletal motion analysis into spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal streams, using channel partitioning to capture distinct movement characteristics efficiently.

arxiv-2501-10527.title: Non-linear equation of motion for higher curvature semiclassical gravity Journal: Physics Letters B
arxiv-2501-10527.creator: Naman Kumar
arxiv-2501-10527.description: Abstract We derive the non-linear semiclassical equation of motion for a general diffeomorphism-invariant theory of gravity by leveraging the thermodynamic properties of closed causal horizons. Our work employs two complementary approaches. The first approach utilizes perturbative quantum gravity applied to a Rindler horizon.

arxiv-2512-19872.title: Spectra for finite unions of line segments Thanks: M. Kolountzakis acknowledges the generous hospitality and support of Fudan University. Thanks: R. Shi is supported by NSFC No. 12571198, NSFC No. 12231013 and the New Cornerstone Science Foundation through the New Cornerstone Investigator Program. T
arxiv-2512-19872.creator: Mihail N. Kolountzakis, Ruxi Shi, Sha Wu
arxiv-2512-19872.description: Abstract . In this paper we study the spectrality of arc-length measures supported on the union of two line segments in the plane. We show that any such spectral measure must admit a line spectrum. Moreover, when the two segments are non-parallel, such spectral measure admits only line spectra. Thus, in this case every spectrum is one dimensional.

arxiv-2601-19844.title: Oscillating Resonances: Imprints of ultralight dark matter at colliders
arxiv-2601-19844.creator: Martin Bauer and Sreemanti Chakraborti
arxiv-2601-19844.description: Abstract In models where ultralight fields constitute dark matter, the misalignment mechanism leads to coherent, low-amplitude oscillations in fundamental constants. This effect arises from effective operators that couple dark matter to Standard Model fields. We present different models that can induce these effective operators by integrating out a mediator field.

pmc-10643473.title: PI3K/AKT signaling activates HIF1α to modulate the biological effects of invasive breast cancer with microcalcification
pmc-10643473.creator: Yao Tian, Lu Zhao, Zhengwei Gui, Shiyang Liu, Chenguang Liu, Tianyao Yu, Lin Zhang
pmc-10643473.description: Microcalcification (MC) is a valuable diagnostic indicator of breast cancer, and it is reported to be associated with increased tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis. Nevertheless, the exact potential molecular mechanism is not completely understood. Here, we find that the mineralized invasive breast cancer (IBC) cells not only increased their proliferation and migration, but also showed the characteristic of doxorubicin resistance.

pmc-10715132.title: Development and validation of a multiplex real-time PCR assay for detection and quantification of Streptococcus pneumoniae in pediatric respiratory samples
pmc-10715132.creator: Molly Butler, Garrett Breazeale, Eric Mwangi, Elaine Dowell, Samuel R. Dominguez, Linda Lamberth, Kristina G. Hultén, Sarah A. Jung
pmc-10715132.description: Streptococcus pneumoniae (Spn) is a bacterial pathogen that causes a range of disease manifestations in children, from acute otitis media to pneumonia, septicemia, and meningitis. Primary Spn laboratory diagnostic identification methods include culture, antigen testing, single-plex real-time PCR, and syndromic PCR panels. However, each method lacks sensitivity, specificity, and/or cost efficiency.

pmc-10990447.title: The effect of individual characteristics on susceptibility to aggressive and/or intimidating approaches: quantifying probability pathways by creating a victimization model
pmc-10990447.creator: Kay de Wit, Melissa Begeman, Wouter Noordkamp, Ilja G Sligte, Rina S Ghafoerkhan, Victor L Kallen
pmc-10990447.description: Background: A significant body of literature has identified multiple factors that contribute to established victimization by aggressive and/or intimidating behaviours. These studies primarily originate from the fields of intimate partner violence (IPV), bullying, sexual abuse, and/or commercial sexual exploitation (CSE), and generally focus on female victims.

pmc-11380203.title: Associations between different insulin resistance indices and the risk of all-cause mortality in peritoneal dialysis patients
pmc-11380203.creator: Guowen Zhao, Sijia Shang, Na Tian, Xiaojiang Zhan, Fenfen Peng, Xiaoyang Wang, Yueqiang Wen, Qingdong Xu, Xiaoran Feng, Xingming Tang, Xianfeng Wu, Qian Zhou, Yuanyuan Yang, Xing Zhang, Ning Su
pmc-11380203.description: BackgroundInsulin resistance (IR) is prevalent in individuals undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) and is related to increased susceptibility to coronary artery disease and initial peritonitis. In recent investigations, correlations have been found between indices of IR and the incidence of all-cause mortality in various populations. However, such correlations have not been detected among individuals undergoing PD.

pmc-11418917.title: Case report from Somalia: access to diagnose retinoblastoma among children in a resource-limited country
pmc-11418917.creator: Abdullahi Ali Roble, Hassan Muhumed Mohamed, Şükran Bekdemir, Yahye Abshir Nor, Said Abdi Mohamed, Asha Abdirahman Yussuf, Ibrahim Ali Hassan, Mohamed Salad Kadiye
pmc-11418917.description: Retinoblastoma, a rare cancer mostly affecting children, makes up ~3% of childhood cancers in developed countries. However, it is more prevalent in sub-Saharan Africa, where late diagnosis often leads to advanced disease and higher mortality rates. Here, we present a 3-year-old girl presented with leukocoria and esotropia in her left eye for 3 months.

pmc-11481106.title: Running shoe cushioning properties at the rearfoot and forefoot and their relationship to injury: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial on leisure-time runners
pmc-11481106.creator: Laurent Malisoux, Axel Urhausen, Nicolas Flores, Daniel Theisen, Cédric Morio
pmc-11481106.description: Previous work has demonstrated the protective effect of shoe cushioning on injury risk in leisure-time runners, but most models currently available on the market have greater cushioning than those investigated so far. Also, the optimal level of cushioning and the role of cushioning on the forepart of the shoe for injury prevention are still unknown.

pmc-11492876.title: BuyangHuanwu Decoction alleviates Endothelial Cell Apoptosis and Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction via Regulation of the MAPKK4/p38 Signaling Axis
pmc-11492876.creator: Xing Chang, Dan Wu, Xin Gao, Jianguo Lin, Ying Tan, Junyan Wang, Hang Zhu, Hao Zhou
pmc-11492876.description: MAPKK4 has been implicated in the pathological mechanisms underlying myocardial and vascular injury, specifically influencing endothelial cell damage and programmed cell death via subcellular pathways. Nevertheless, the regulatory role of MAPKK4 in coronary microvascular injury following myocardial infarction remains unconfirmed, and the exploration of targeted mitochondrial protective therapeutic agents remains unaddressed.

pmc-11565396.title: A fatty acid-ordered plasma membrane environment is critical for Ebola virus matrix protein assembly and budding
pmc-11565396.creator: Souad Amiar, Kristen A Johnson, Monica L Husby, Andrea Marzi, Robert V Stahelin
pmc-11565396.description: Plasma membrane (PM) domains and order phases have been shown to play a key role in the assembly, release, and entry of several lipid-enveloped viruses. In the present study, we provide a mechanistic understanding of the Ebola virus (EBOV) matrix protein VP40 interaction with PM lipids and their effect on VP40 oligomerization, a crucial step for viral assembly and budding.

pmc-12565221.title: Improving Telenomus remus (Hymenoptera: Scelionidae) Adoption: Contribution of Different Egg Parasitoid Densities, Fed Adults, and Their Storage for Successful Biological Control of Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
pmc-12565221.creator: Weidson P Sutil, Adeney de F Bueno, Leonardo Roswadoski, Rafael S Iasczczaki, Gabriel S Carneiro, Yelitza C Colmenarez, Nuray Baser, Gulay Kacar, Dragana Šunjka
pmc-12565221.description: Simple SummaryEmploying beneficial insects to control crop pests is a sustainable alternative to chemical pesticides, but some important questions remain for their successful use in the field. For instance, how many Telenomus remus (Hymenoptera: Scelionidae) should be released to effectively reduce Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) populations, and how to keep them alive and healthy before release remains unclear. T.

pmc-12604193.title: Ring-and-flap: a novel and accessible alternative to fix-and-flap in Gustilo IIIB-C open tibia fractures (an institutional experience)
pmc-12604193.creator: Jonathan Yeo, Jeremy Mingfa Sun, Ing How Moo, Wei Yuan, Ho Chin Boo, Andy Kuei Siong Yeo
pmc-12604193.description: BackgroundThe fix-and-flap regime is resource intense and may not be readily available. As an alternative, the ring fixator serves as a versatile option for limb salvage, however it poses challenges to soft tissue reconstruction due to the limited working space around the rings and pins.

pmc-13362036.title: Computational Method Using Attribute-Aware Message Passing and Graph Convolutional Network for Potential miRNA–Disease Association Prediction
pmc-13362036.creator: Peng Qin, Jiyong An
pmc-13362036.description: MicroRNA (miRNA) dysregulation is a crucial pathogenic factor that extensively participates in the occurrence and progression of various human diseases, especially cancers. Identifying unknown miRNA–disease connections is essential for understanding disease pathogenesis and improving clinical treatment strategies. Traditional biological experiments are often expensive and technically restricted, so computational prediction has become a widely used auxiliary research tool.

pmc-13498429.title: Prolonged Episodes of Paroxysmal Exertion-Induced Dystonia in Glut1 Deficiency Syndrome
pmc-13498429.creator: Joerg Klepper, Lucia Kiesel, Eva Runkel

pmc-13556639.title: 849. To avoid or not to avoid? Prefrontal integration of cortical inputs modulates extinction of avoidance
pmc-13556639.creator: G J Quirk
pmc-13556639.description: BackgroundThe medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) has a well-established role in extinction learning, triggering plasticity and cellular inhibition via projections to the amygdala. Simple behavioral models such auditory threat (fear) conditioning demonstrate how the infralimbic (IL) mPFC inhibits amygdala output during extinction learning, which is a key component of cognitive behavioral therapies for anxiety disorders.

pmc-13606569.title: Integrating Metabolomics and Network Pharmacology to Identify Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors from Raspberry Leaf: Optimization by Ultrasound-Assisted Extraction and Kinetic Characterization
pmc-13606569.creator: Zuoming Cao, Yan Wang, Yonghui Zhang, Zuoting Yang, Jun Sheng, Yang Tian, Lei Peng
pmc-13606569.description: The rising global prevalence of hyperuricemia has intensified the search for natural xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibitors from food-grade botanicals. This study screened leaf extracts from four plant species for XO inhibitory activity and identified raspberry leaf as the most potent source. Among seven extraction and pre-treatment methods, ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) outperformed conventional decoction and all alternatives.

pmc-13649807.title: Hybrid Surgery for Urethral Diverticulum Penetrating the Bladder
pmc-13649807.creator: Yugo Sawada, Yasuhide Kitagawa, Kojiro Nishio, Tokumasa Hayashi, Shino Tokiwa, Mika Nagae, Masayoshi Jimmy Nomura
pmc-13649807.description: Introduction and HypothesisUrethral diverticula have various morphological patterns, and in complex cases, a transvaginal approach can be difficult. MethodsHere, we report a case in which a urethral diverticulum originating from the ventral (posterior) side of the urethra penetrated the bladder through the diverticular wall.

pmc-13667573.title: An Innovative Decoupled Spatio-Vertical–Temporal Learning Model Based on Topography Guidance for Wind Vector Forecasting
pmc-13667573.creator: Xinyu Liu, Huan Li, Xinyue Mo
pmc-13667573.description: Highlights What are the main findings? TG-SVTFormer improves multi-step wind speed forecasting by decoupling spatiotemporal features and preserving fine spatial details.Integrating topography and upper-air states adds physical constraints, reducing long-horizon prediction errors. What are the implications of the main findings? Accurate fine-grained wind forecasts over complex terrain support secure grid integration and smart dispatching.
